name: Drawer
summary: A drawer is a panel that slides in from an edge of the screen and sits above the page. Use it for filters, a menu, or anything that would crowd the layout it belongs to. It is almost entirely focus management: focus moves in on open, is trapped while the drawer is modal, and returns to the trigger on close.
demoNote: Open any of these and press Tab repeatedly: in the first three, focus cannot leave. Tab straight out of the fourth, which is the one that does not claim to be modal.

contract.useWhen: A panel from a screen edge. The whole component is the focus management.
keyboard: cycles inside — it is trapped while the drawer is modal
native: activates the trigger, which toggles the drawer
closes, and focus returns to the trigger
failureModes: focus left behind on the page, so the next Tab starts from the top
no visible close control, which is a trap on touch where there is no Escape key
popover=auto light dismiss fighting a custom Escape handler — use manual
overflow:hidden alone for the scroll lock, which jumps the layout sideways
role=listbox on the drawer itself, instead of leaving its contents their own semantics
api: AC.createDrawer(root, options) -> { open, close, isOpen, isModal, element, destroy }
